newsitem.title: USA: Houston voters approve $265 million stadium.
newsitem.headline: Houston voters approve $265 million stadium.

text.p: A proposal to build a new baseball stadium in central Houston was approved by voters on Tuesday, making it likely the Houston Astros professional baseball team will remain in the city.
Election officials said the proposition passed by a margin of 51 percent to 49 percent after an intense battle between local leaders who supported it and anti-tax groups.
Harris County officials now will move forward with plans to build a $265 million stadium with a retractable dome. Supporters say the stadium will bring new life to the city's downtown area.
Houston Astros owner Drayton McLane had said a new stadium was necessary if the team was to stay in the city. The Astros currently play at the Astrodome, which opened in 1965.
The new facility will be financed partly by the private sector but mostly by sales taxes which still must be approved by the Texas state legislature.
